ORDINANCE I OF 1998

FRONTIER PROVINCE ECONOMIC AND
FINANCIAL REFORMS
ORDINANCE, 1998
ORDINANCE I OF 1998
An Ordinance to provide for securing economic life and
financial stability in the North-West Frontier Province
[Gazette of N.-W.F.P.
Extraordinary, 11th June, 1998]
No. Legis: 1(5)/98, dated
11-6-1998.--The following Ordinance by the Governor of the North-West
Frontier Province is hereby published for general, information:---
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.--(1) This Ordinance may be called the North-West Frontier
Province Economic and Financial Reforms Ordinance, 1998.
(2) It shall extend to whole of
the North-West Frontier Province.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

sections.shortTitle: N -W F P Economic and Financial Reforms Ordinance 1998
sections.description:
Protection of financial stability

ORDINANCE I OF 1998
NORTH-WEST
FRONTIER PROVINCE ECONOMIC AND
FINANCIAL REFORMS
ORDINANCE, 1998
ORDINANCE I OF 1998
An Ordinance to provide for securing economic life and
financial stability in the North-West Frontier Province
[Gazette of N.-W.F.P.
Extraordinary, 11th June, 1998]
No. Legis: 1(5)/98, dated
11-6-1998.--The following Ordinance by the Governor of the North-West
Frontier Province is hereby published for general, information:---
3. Protection of financial
stability.--(1) Notwithstanding anything to contrary contained in any law
for the time being in force, Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette or in such other manner as it may deem fit, take such measures, issue
such directions and frame such policies and schemes as it considers to be
necessary to improve the economic life and financial stability in the Province
with particular reference to its developmental and non developmental
expenditures.
(2) Without prejudice to the
generality of the foregoing provisions, a step taken under subsection (1) may
provide for all or any of the following matters:
(i) abolition of services,
departments or posts not being useful to public purposes;
(ii) improvement in office
management through automation;
(iii) private sector
participation--management of affairs on BOO, BLT and BOT basis;
(iv) introduction of management
concept of existing services on contract basis;
(v) simplified tax assessment and
tax collection system;
(vi) managerial and financial
autonomy to units like Lady Reading Hospital, Hayat Shaheed Teaching Hospital
and Hayat Abad Medical Complex at Peshawar, Ayub Medical Complex, Abbottabad,
Postgraduate/Degree Colleges, Universities and other public utility
institutions/units in various fields under Government;
(vii) privatization of public sector
industrial units;
(viii) disposal of public sector
properties including Government buildings, shops, rest house, hotels, etc.,
through auction in a transparent manner;
(ix) disposal of State land
through open auction with first right of refusal to the sitting tenants;
(x) disposal or leasing out of
Government owned machinery;
(xi) disposal of surplus
Government vehicles through open auction;
(xii) retirement of debt from the
revenue generated from disposal of Government properties, assets, machinery,
etc;
(xiii) community participation in
construction, maintenance and operation of schemes such as water supply,
irrigation, education, health and other Government schemes;
(xiv) privatization of Government
institutions in various sectors, such as education health. etc, which can be
operated more efficiently, effectively and economically in the private sector;
(xv) restructuring and
consolidation of Government, local councils and other autonomous bodies for
increased self-sustained and self-reliant operation; and
(xvi) such other matters as
Government may deem fit for achieving the object of economic and financial
reforms.
(3) No action taken under the
preceding subsections shall be called in question in any Court or before any.
Authority and shall, for all intents and purposes, be deemed to be lawfully
taken and shall stand protected in perpetuity.

4. Removal of disparity
between developmental and non developmental budgets.--Government shall
gradually reduce the gap proportionately through each financial year-between
the developmental and non -developmental expenditures, so as to bring the ratio
to 40:60 by the year two thousand two.
